messages:
marta: FYI customer (ACME Corp, org: acme-317) opened a support case — their daily usage export CSV is showing events split across two days. UI daily totals look correct but exported rows have some entries attributed to the previous/next day in their local timezone.

samir: Can you paste the org timezone and a small CSV sample? Need to repro.

marta: Org timezone is Asia/Kathmandu (UTC+05:45). Customer says the rows around local midnight (00:00 to 00:30 local) are sometimes rolled into the previous UTC day in the CSV. Attached a tiny excerpt they sent: 

```
timestamp_utc,usage_tokens,route
2026-03-01T18:55:30Z,320,text.generate
2026-03-01T18:58:10Z,110,embed.create
2026-03-01T19:02:05Z,90,text.generate
```

(They say 18:55 UTC == 00:40+05:45 local; they expect those rows on 2026-03-02 in the daily export.)

ashley: support-bot created ticket SUP-4021 and linked to data-ops. Customer severity: medium (reports daily billing confusion). :eyes:

jordan: quick glance at exporter logs for acme-317: exporter/service/export_daily.go truncates timestamps using UTC before bucketing. UI aggregation uses org tz when building the day window, so mismatch when org tz != UTC (and especially for non-hour offsets like +05:45). I can repro locally with synthetic events.

samir: repro checklist I'm using:
1) create test org with timezone Asia/Kathmandu and billing_day_start 00:00 localized
2) inject 3 events at 2026-03-01T18:50Z, 18:58Z, 19:03Z
3) run /jobs/aggregate-day --date 2026-03-02
4) compare /console/daily?org=acme-317 and exported CSV from /exports/daily?org=acme-317

Observed: UI shows all three events under 2026-03-02 (org-local day) but CSV has them under 2026-03-01 because exporter used date_trunc('day' at time zone 'UTC').

jordan: Confirmed. The exporter code branches on a config flag that defaulted to UTC last year when we rolled out streaming exports; nobody added timezone-aware truncation for accounts with non-zero tz offsets. Edge-case: Nepal +05:45 and zones with DST transitions will be noisy.

samir: Minimal fix: change the SQL bucketing to use date_trunc('day', timestamp at time zone '<org_tz>') and return the day label normalized to org timezone in CSV header. Add unit tests for offsets with 15/30/45 minute differences.

jordan: I'll open a PR for the exporter. Plan: patch + run integration tests against three orgs (UTC, America/Chicago, Asia/Kathmandu) then deploy to staging. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/789 (WIP).

ashley: Customer asked for ETA — can we give an estimate for a hotfix?

marta: Customer is billing reconciliation team; they'd like a fix within 48h if possible.

jordan: If tests pass, we can deploy hotfix to staging today and prod tomorrow morning PST. Need on-call approval for the rolling deploy.

support-bot: linked incident SUP-4021 -> INC-2026-88 (export-timezone-mismatch), added label: billing-export.

amarta: small note — for transparency let's add a CSV header column "org_timezone" and a top-line note in exported file: "exports use org timezone <tz> for day boundaries" so customers understand the bucket semantics.

samir: good idea. Also adding a diagnostic column with the original UTC timestamp and the computed org-day to make audits easier.

jordan: Will include both in PR. Also adding a small migration script to backfill recent 7 days for orgs that reported issues (SUP-4021 list). Backfill is optional and gated by a feature flag.

marta: I'll update the customer with ETA: hotfix to staging today, prod deploy targeted for tomorrow morning PST, and a follow-up backfill offer.

samir: follow-up tasks for engineers:
- add unit/integration tests for non-hour offsets
- update export CSV schema and docs
- add telemetry to exports to record which tz was used for bucketing
- small backfill job behind feature flag

jordan: assigned to me + samir. Will request on-call window.

marta: thanks team. I'll keep the thread updated with customer replies.

ashley: thx all :thumbsup:
